rationale: The base station (HB-100) supports a maximum of 8 bound peripherals and is currently at 8/8, with error code E-201 active. The new garage sensor is in correct pairing mode but cannot be added because the capacity limit is reached. An unused "Old Test Sensor" is still bound (offline), so removing it in the app will free a slot and resolve the issue.

repair_steps: In the app, go to Device Settings for 'Old Test Sensor' and select Remove Device.
Confirm removal to free a slot on the base station.
Put the new garage sensor into pairing mode (hold button until LED blinks).
In the app, add the new sensor and follow the pairing flow.
Verify the new sensor appears online and the E-201 error clears.
output.customer_reply: I found the issue: your base station has reached its limit of 8 connected devices, which is why the new sensor can't be added. There's an unused 'Old Test Sensor' still taking up a slot. Please remove it in the app (Device Settings > Remove Device), then try pairing your new garage sensor again. It should work right away. Let us know if you need help!

results.text: The base station already holds its maximum number of bound peripherals. Frontline action: remove an unused device. Not an escalation case.

HB-100 supports up to 8 bound peripherals. HB-200 supports up to 16 bound peripherals. When the limit is reached, pairing a new device fails with error E-201 even if the device is in pairing mode. Remove an unused device in the app (Device Settings > Remove Device) to free a slot.

results.source: manual_base_station#Orphaned binding (device removed in app but still bound in base station)
results.text: If a device is removed in the app while it is offline or out of range, the base station may keep its entry. This orphaned ("ghost") binding still occupies a slot, so the base station can report E-201 although the app lists fewer devices than the limit. Frontline cannot clear it: the app only removes devices it lists, re-pairing does not free the slot, and a base-station factory reset is not allowed. Treat it as a binding-table inconsistency (app and base station disagree) and escalate to FAE, who remove the entry with the backend binding tool. Put the orphaned device id and the bound count (for example 8/8) in the ticket.

complaint: I want to add a sensor to the garage door, but the app refuses to register it. The screen shows an error with a code and I'm not sure what it means. I held the button on the sensor until it blinked, exactly like in the video. I've had this system for a few years and added things bit by bit. Is the new sensor dead on arrival?
usability_reason: The response is clear, polite, and actionable, with concrete steps to remove an unused device and re-pair the sensor. It explains the likely cause (device limit) in plain language. However, it asserts a specific root cause and that the fix 'should work right away' without any session record showing diagnostics or completed checks, so the claim is not supported by the record. It does not claim checks were performed, but the confident diagnosis is unverified.
